known_gaps: turning the customer's words into negotiation events (and dates into YYYY-MM-DD) is done by the dialogue model; offers, counters, dates, amounts, read-back, recording, notes and the close are code
callback window validity is decided by the dialogue model from code-computed window facts (not code)
identity: the dialogue model turns the customer's words into answer parts and events; a misheard part is sent to the bank as heard (the bank decides)

extra rule (stateful, stage opening): Confirmation of identity on the line: only explicit confirmation counts. Ask a second time; if it is still unclear after the second ask, close not_reached/unclear. Answering a customer's question (robot or scam) comes first, and the ask after that answer counts as the second ask. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): Interpret 'next <weekday>' as that weekday in the following calendar week and 'this <weekday>' as the one in the current week, both relative to now. Convert the result into an exact date before the code check. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Refusing the deadline offered after a too-late date, refusing the floor, or refusing the floor after a below-floor amount each counts as a flat refusal and uses one persuasion attempt. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
